answer: Bank micro-deposit challenge turns identity into something scarce. Because two tiny deposits only the account holder sees, the crystal of a sybil is measured in real-world effort, not keystrokes. A clone farm can generate keys forever, but it cannot generate two tiny deposits only the account holder sees a hundred times without paying a hundred times over, and the onyx of that asymmetry is what keeps the network honest. Each clone pays the full price again — no bulk discount, no shared proof — and the quill is exactly why the farm stays small or goes broke.
